promises.promise: Who is in the household, which agents they own, and which projects they share. Everything else in loom points back at these three: members, agents and projects.
Lists the members: people who can sign in.
Lists the agents, and who owns each.
Puts people and agents on projects so they can work together.
Supplies the labels every other part uses to decide who sees what.
A pull request gets its project from its repository.
Every conversation belongs to one agent.
An item can be for one member alone.
Every task has an owner. Without a project, its owner decides who sees it.
A token says which member or agent is calling.
A box's owner says which agents may run there.
A member is a person who can sign in. A household owner sees everything, including another member's private thread. Everyone else reaches things through their projects and the agents they own.

An agent is one of the household's assistants. A member owns any number of agents, and an agent can have more than one owner. Each agent has a short description of itself, badge colours and a drawn face.
A project is the unit of sharing. Put a person and an agent on the same project and they can work together on it. A project also lists its code repositories.
One row holds the household-wide settings. Each person has their own preferences for how loom looks and behaves.
a The rule. A household owner sees everything, including what is private to another member. Anyone else sees what is in their projects, plus what belongs to agents they own.
b Private. Private to a member means that member plus household owners.
c Tasks. A task with a project is seen by the project's people. A task without one is seen by its owner, and for an agent's task, by that agent's owners.
d Checked at the door. Loom applies this to callers from outside: a person, an agent, a machine, someone's own program. Loom's own parts read without asking.
The owner can open project sharing without an unavailable screen.
The owner can open household members and agents without an unavailable screen.
Adding a household member through the normal built program persists that member.
Creating a project through the normal built program persists its member list.
